Aatrox.watch: Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade’s sweet spots and knock-up are dangerous, so when you see the cast animation, move outside the edge of its range or close in toward the center. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, move out of its area immediately instead of stopping to choose a direction before being pulled. When Aatrox R World Ender is active, his healing increases, so create distance and let its duration run out.
Aatrox.build: Build armor first to prepare for Aatrox’s main damage from Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade and Aatrox W Infernal Chains.
Aatrox.fight: Avoid direct fights early, and look to trade just after Aatrox uses his Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance empowered attack on a minion. Close the gap after Aatrox E Umbral Dash is down, then use Nasus W Wither to catch him and fight. If Aatrox R World Ender is active, don’t accept a duel; back off, then re-engage.
Aatrox.laning: Focus on not giving up a kill early. If Aatrox pushes the lane, farm safely near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire, since it pushes the lane and uses mana. If the pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Aatrox.combo: In fights, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Aatrox in E’s area with W, then use Q after E lowers his armor so your physical damage is more effective.
Aatrox.escape: The moment after Aatrox uses Aatrox E Umbral Dash is your chance to close the gap. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains is also down, use Nasus W Wither to slow him and move in while there’s less risk of being pulled.
Aatrox.phase: In the mid game, look for fights when you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands ready, but back off if Aatrox R World Ender is active. In the late game, fight head-on with your accumulated stacks or split push to pressure a turret.
Aatrox.teamfight: Don’t lead the engage alone; go in after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry or whoever is diving your back line, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on targets in Nasus E Spirit Fire. Activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands when the teamfight starts to deal area damage and chain Q attacks.

Akali.watch: Prioritize dodging the first projectile from Akali E Shuriken Flip. If it marks you, the second dash will follow you even if you try to escape, so don’t force a fight while marked. The second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution gets stronger based on your missing health, so be especially careful when your health is low.
Akali.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for Akali’s main damage. Get enough health to survive the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution, and get movement speed to leave its telegraphed area.
Akali.fight: Prioritize Q last hits early, and trade back when Akali comes out of Akali W Twilight Shroud to attack. It’s a good time to fight aggressively after you dodge the first projectile from Akali E Shuriken Flip and while Akali R Perfect Execution is still down. In small skirmishes, look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Akali goes in.
Akali.combo: In fights, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Akali in E’s area with W, then use Q after E reduces her armor. Look for a chance to hit Akali with Nasus E Spirit Fire when she briefly becomes visible inside Akali W Twilight Shroud.
Akali.escape: Don’t go in immediately just because either Akali W Twilight Shroud or Akali E Shuriken Flip is down. Dodge the first projectile from Akali E Shuriken Flip, check whether her other escape tools are down, and go in especially before Akali R Perfect Execution returns.
Akali.phase: Nasus gets stronger in the mid to late game as you build stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands.
Akali.teamfight: Don’t go in first alone; engage after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on targets in Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Akali targets your back line, use W on her to slow her.

Tryndamere.watch: When Tryndamere P Battle Fury builds up, his critical hits become dangerous, so create distance while he builds Fury by attacking minions. If Tryndamere E Spinning Slash brings him in, reduce his movement speed and attack speed with Nasus W Wither. While Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, don’t pour in damage; create distance and wait out its duration.
Tryndamere.build: Build armor first because Tryndamere’s main damage is physical. Thornmail is effective against an opponent who relies on basic attacks, and if his healing is a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Tryndamere.combo: In fights, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Tryndamere on the area with Nasus W Wither, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Tryndamere.escape: The moment after you make Tryndamere use Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is your chance to close the gap or catch him. When backing off, walk backward while facing Tryndamere to avoid the slow from Tryndamere W Mocking Shout. If you are hit by Tryndamere W Mocking Shout, your attack damage is reduced, so don’t immediately start a basic-attack fight.
Tryndamere.fight: Early on, avoid head-on fights and build Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks. After Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, catch him with Nasus W Wither and hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. In small skirmishes, it’s better to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after the opponent goes in.
Tryndamere.laning: Don’t push the lane aggressively; last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret. Under your turret, don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire so you preserve your last hits and mana. If Tryndamere’s heavy pressure makes even last hits difficult, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Tryndamere.phase: In the mid to late game, your accumulated stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands make you strong in head-on fights. In the late game, you can push a side lane with your stacks and pressure a turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Tryndamere.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies engage. If Tryndamere goes after your back line, catch him with Nasus W Wither, then hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, don’t pour in more damage; create distance and wait out its duration.

Skarner.escape: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is Skarner’s mobility tool, so right after he uses it is your chance to engage. If a wall collision causes a stun, Skarner E Ixtal's Impact comes back sooner, so retreat while accounting for his re-engage. While Skarner R Impale is available, don’t engage on the assumption that you can escape after being caught.
Skarner.build: First decide whether you need a way to remove the suppression from Skarner R Impale, and consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar if needed. Build magic resistance first against the damage from Skarner P Threads of Vibration, Skarner W Seismic Bastion, and Skarner R Impale. He also deals damage based on your maximum health, so prioritize movement speed and defensive stats over relying on a large health increase.
Skarner.combo: After Skarner E Ixtal’s Impact is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Skarner on E with W, then hit Q after E’s armor reduction applies.
Skarner.fight: Close the gap and fight right after Skarner uses Skarner E Ixtal’s Impact. Catch Skarner with Nasus W Wither and hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. In small skirmishes, look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Skarner goes in.
Skarner.laning: If Skarner pushes the lane, collect the wave near your turret, and don’t push the lane with Nasus E Spirit Fire during that time. If your Q last hits keep getting denied, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Skarner.phase: In mid game, fight during a window when Skarner E Ixtal’s Impact is down, using your accumulated stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Nasus gets strong with stacks in the late game, but Skarner also becomes tankier and better at catching you as he gets items, so keep managing your distance.
Skarner.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies start the fight. If Skarner goes after your back line, slow him with Nasus W Wither, and hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire during the fight. Check your position around the edges of the Dragon or Baron pit, since Skarner R Impale can drag you through terrain.
Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal’s Impact dashes through terrain, stuns the target when he slams them into a wall, and lets him re-engage sooner, so don’t stand with your back to a wall. If Skarner R Impale grabs you, you can’t escape with a movement ability, so keep your distance from its range and from Skarner’s allies. After he gets close, Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval’s empowered basic attacks and Skarner P Threads of Vibration damage follow, so manage distance first.

Kayle.build: First, focus on stacking last hits with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, and build magic resistance against Kayle’s magic damage. If the healing from Kayle W Celestial Blessing becomes a problem, fit in Executioner's Calling.
Kayle.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Slow Kayle with W to keep her on E, then land Q after E reduces her armor. If Kayle R Divine Judgment is active, wait for the right moment to deal Q damage.
Kayle.escape: Engage when Kayle Q Radiant Blast’s slow is down or you dodge the direct hit. Kayle can use Kayle W Celestial Blessing to gain movement speed and escape, so if you have a chance to stick to her, use Nasus W Wither to chase.
Kayle.laning: If Kayle pushes the lane, let it come to you and take last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the wave or spend mana on Nasus E Spirit Fire here. If you can’t farm, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Kayle.teamfight: Don’t lead the charge alone. After your team starts the fight, enter from a flank or an unseen route that lets you reach Kayle. Use Nasus W Wither to reduce Kayle’s movement and attack speed, and time it with your allies’ crowd control. After Kayle R Divine Judgment’s damage immunity ends, land Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Kayle.watch: Kayle Q Radiant Blast slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, so avoid taking it directly. When you have lost health, watch out for Kayle E Starfire Spellblade, which deals damage based on your missing health. Don’t pour in damage while Kayle R Divine Judgment is active.

Kled.build: Build armor first to withstand Kled’s main damage. Since Nasus has no mobility, you can prioritize tenacity against Kled’s chain crowd control. Even if you build damage, include a defensive item such as Dead Man's Plate.
Kled.combo: In a fight, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W to reduce Kled’s movement and attack speed and keep him on E, then reduce his armor with E before landing Q.
Kled.escape: If you’re caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, immediately create distance before you’re pulled in. When engaging, look for an opening after Kled E Jousting and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! are down. If only one is down, account for the other mobility tool.
Kled.fight: Early on, avoid extended fights with Kled and stack Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. When Kled W Violent Tendencies activates, back off before taking four hits, then go back in. In skirmishes, wait for Kled to engage, then activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and fight back.
Kled.laning: If Kled pushes the lane, farm near your turret and last hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the wave or spend mana on Nasus E Spirit Fire here. If Kled’s pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Kled.phase: Direct fights become strong from the mid-to-late game, once you have stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Kled gets weaker after the laning phase and mid game, so the longer the game goes, the better it is for Nasus.
Kled.teamfight: Use flank vision to spot Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! coming in. If you can’t stop it, keep a formation where your front line takes the hit first. Don’t lead the charge alone; after your team starts the fight, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and go in. Use Nasus W Wither to pin down the enemy carry, then hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Kled.watch: If you’re caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, create distance before the pull triggers. When Kled W Violent Tendencies is active, back off to avoid the fourth attack’s damage based on maximum health. Also watch for Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! coming from out of vision.

Quinn.teamfight: Don’t lead the charge alone; enter after your team starts the fight. If Quinn flanks, use Nasus W Wither to pin her down, then hit Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Ward Quinn’s roaming routes and encourage your team to fight together.
Quinn.build: Build armor first against Quinn's damage. Even if you focus on damage, include a defensive item such as Dead Man's Plate.
Quinn.combo: After Quinn E Vault is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W to keep Quinn in E's range, then hit her with Q after E reduces her armor.
Quinn.escape: Quinn E Vault is her escape, so immediately after she uses it is your chance to close the distance. Don't rush in before then; once E is down, hold Quinn with Nasus W Wither.
Quinn.fight: Early on, don't approach first without jungle help; start trading when Quinn E Vault is down or your jungler arrives. Use Nasus W Wither to reduce Quinn's movement and attack speed, then hit her with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while she is on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Quinn.laning: Preserve your health early and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If Quinn pushes the wave, farm near your turret and don't use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push it. If you can't even get Q last hits, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Quinn.phase: Nasus gets stronger in the mid to late game with his stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, but if your farming is denied, your growth will also be delayed.
Quinn.watch: When marked by Quinn P Harrier, move outside her range to avoid the empowered basic attack. Dodge Quinn Q Blinding Assault from behind the minion wave, and don't force an approach while Quinn E Vault is available.

Aurora.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for Aurora’s damage. Aurora P Spirit Abjuration deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building only health, and get movement speed to escape area attacks. If the healing from Aurora P Spirit Abjuration is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Aurora.combo: When Aurora is visible and you can catch her, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Aurora in Nasus E Spirit Fire with Nasus W Wither, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after her armor is reduced. If Aurora is stealthed with Aurora W Across the Veil, don’t use targeted abilities; wait for her to become visible.
Aurora.escape: Don’t go in just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down; also watch Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora R Between Worlds. If both Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora W Across the Veil are down, and Aurora R Between Worlds hasn’t returned, use Nasus W Wither to catch her.
Aurora.fight: Avoid forcing trades early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If health has dropped while Aurora Q Twofold Hex is on you, retreat instead of trying to tank the recall damage. When fighting, wait until Aurora’s mobility is down, then catch her with Nasus W Wither and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Aurora.laning: If Aurora pushes the lane, farm near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the lane or spend mana. If the pressure makes even last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Aurora.phase: From the mid game onward, Nasus gets stronger once you have built stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so look for a fight when Aurora’s mobility is down. In the late game, join teamfights or use your accumulated stacks to pressure a turret.
Aurora.teamfight: Don’t go in first alone; engage after your team starts the fight. If Aurora leaps in but doesn’t get a takedown, catch her with Nasus W Wither and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Aurora gets a takedown, her leap cooldown resets, so don’t leave low-health allies behind as you retreat.
Aurora.watch: Aurora Q Twofold Hex deals damage again when recalled, and that damage increases as your health gets lower. If you’re cursed, move out of the line between Aurora and yourself, and if your health is marginal, retreat before the recall. Decide whether to leave before Aurora R Between Worlds appears or fight inside the area.

Camille.build: Build armor first to prepare for Camille’s main damage, and get enough health to survive the true damage from Camille Q Precision Protocol. Camille W Tactical Sweep deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building only health. If you need more survivability, fit in an item like Dead Man’s Plate; if healing from Camille W Tactical Sweep is a problem, consider Executioner’s Calling.
Camille.combo: After Camille P Adaptive Defenses’ shield disappears, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Camille in Nasus E Spirit Fire with Nasus W Wither, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after her armor is reduced.
Camille.escape: The window to go in is after Camille E Hookshot is down and before Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum returns. If only one is down, she can escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage. When you go in, use Nasus W Wither to slow Camille.
Camille.fight: Avoid forced trades early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Back off just after Camille P Adaptive Defenses’ shield activates, then fight with Nasus W Wither after the shield disappears to reduce her movement and attack speed. If Camille goes in during a small skirmish, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and follow up with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Camille.laning: Stand away from walls and among your minions. If Camille pushes the lane, farm near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Using Nasus E Spirit Fire can push the lane and make you miss last hits, so save mana for fights and gank follow-ups. If the pressure keeps you from building stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Camille.phase: Camille is weak before her first core item, but Nasus needs to build stacks to gain an advantage as the game goes on. From the mid game onward, Camille can take turrets quickly, so don’t leave the side lane unattended. In the late game, once you have stacks, look for fights with Nasus R Fury of the Sands ready.
Camille.teamfight: Don’t go in first alone; engage after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry to slow them, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Camille targets your back line, catch her with Nasus W Wither. When the teamfight starts, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands to deal area damage and follow up with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot uses walls to engage from long range and stun you, so stand away from walls and don’t let yourself get pushed toward one. If you’re trapped by Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum, don’t waste Nasus W Wither as she casts it; wait out the area’s duration, then counterattack.

Chogath.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for Cho’Gath Q Rupture, W Feral Scream, and E Vorpal Spikes, and consider tenacity. Resistance cannot reduce the true damage from Cho’Gath R Feast, and Cho’Gath E Vorpal Spikes deals damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about building only health. If healing from Cho’Gath P Carnivore is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Chogath.combo: While Cho’Gath Q Rupture is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Cho’Gath in the area with Nasus W Wither, lower his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Chogath.escape: The moment after Cho’Gath uses Cho’Gath Q Rupture on the wave is your chance to go in. Close the gap while avoiding the frontal silence from Cho’Gath W Feral Scream, then slow him with Nasus W Wither. Create distance if you’re caught by Cho’Gath Q Rupture or your health gets low enough to be threatened by Cho’Gath R Feast.
Chogath.fight: Look for a trade after dodging Cho’Gath Q Rupture or right after he uses it on the wave. Approach from the side to avoid Cho’Gath’s front, then catch him with Nasus W Wither and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. In small skirmishes, also look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Cho’Gath goes in.
Chogath.laning: Don’t push the lane recklessly early; let the wave come to you and secure last hits and stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Stand off the line Cho’Gath attacks along so Cho’Gath E Vorpal Spikes doesn’t pierce through you along with the minions. Near your turret, don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the lane, and if even last hits are difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Chogath.phase: In the mid game, look for an opening while Cho’Gath Q Rupture is down when you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands ready. In the late game, accumulated stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands make Nasus strong in direct fights, but Cho’Gath also becomes more durable with Feast stacks, so don’t stay in range of Cho’Gath R Feast when your health is low.
Chogath.teamfight: Don’t lead the engage alone; go in after your team starts the fight. Activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry to slow them, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If you see the tell for Cho’Gath Q Rupture, dodge to the side, and if health drops, leave the range of Cho’Gath R Feast.
Chogath.watch: When the tell for Cho’Gath Q Rupture appears beneath you, immediately move to the side to dodge it. Cho’Gath W Feral Scream silences you from the front, making it hard to dodge the follow-up Cho’Gath Q Rupture, so avoid trading head-on. If your health is at or below half, move out of range of Cho’Gath R Feast, which deals true damage.

Darius.build: Build armor first to prepare for Darius’s physical damage, and fit in survivability items like Dead Man’s Plate so you can withstand focused attacks even with Nasus R Fury of the Sands active. Darius E Apprehend pierces some armor, and Darius R Noxian Guillotine deals true damage, so get health as well. If healing from Darius Q Decimate is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Darius.combo: After Darius E Apprehend is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Darius in Nasus E Spirit Fire with W, then use Q after E reduces his armor to increase your physical damage.
Darius.escape: The window to engage first is when Darius E Apprehend misses or is on cooldown. Create distance if Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up or Darius E Apprehend becomes available.
Darius.fight: Avoid long fights early, and trade briefly after Darius E Apprehend misses or just after he uses Darius Q Decimate to clear minions. When closing in, slow Darius with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Darius P Hemorrhage stacks are building, break off and look for another chance after they disappear.
Darius.laning: At this point, don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the lane; save mana for fights or gank follow-ups. If the pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Darius.phase: Nasus gets stronger in the mid to late game with stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, but avoid fights that let Darius build up bleed stacks for a long time. In the late game, you can fight with your accumulated Q stacks or split push to pressure a turret.
Darius.teamfight: Don’t go in first alone; engage after your team starts the fight. If Darius targets your back line, catch him with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Darius kills you with Darius R Noxian Guillotine while you have several bleed stacks, its cooldown resets, so get out of range if health has dropped.
Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, it leads into Darius W Crippling Strike and Darius Q Decimate, so wait outside its range. When you see Darius Q Decimate, leave the blade’s range or stay close to his body to reduce its damage and healing. If Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, create distance. If you have several stacks and health has dropped, get completely out of range of Darius R Noxian Guillotine.

DrMundo.build: Build armor first to mitigate the physical damage from Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If healing makes the duel drag on, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
DrMundo.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Dr. Mundo in E’s area with W, then land Q after E reduces his armor.
DrMundo.escape: Dr. Mundo has no ability to create distance on his own, so catch him with Nasus W Wither when you have an opening to engage. Dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw from behind minions, and look to fight while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down.
DrMundo.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. When fighting, slow Dr. Mundo’s movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither, then use Q in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. Look for an opening while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down.
DrMundo.phase: Direct fights get stronger from the mid to late game, once you have stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands. If Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, look for advantages elsewhere instead of spending time trying to kill him.
DrMundo.teamfight: Don’t engage first on your own; go in after your allies initiate. Cast Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If you activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands at the start of a teamfight, it deals damage over time around you and lets you land Q repeatedly.
DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw hits the first target it reaches and deals damage based on current health, so be especially careful when your health is high and stand behind minions.

Fiora.build: Build armor first to withstand the physical damage from Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework. Resistance can’t reduce the true damage from Fiora P Duelist’s Dance or Fiora R Grand Challenge, and she also deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building only health.
Fiora.combo: After confirming Fiora W Riposte is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Fiora in the area with Nasus W Wither, reduce her armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land an empowered attack.
Fiora.escape: The moment after you make Fiora use Fiora Q Lunge is your chance to close the gap. If Fiora W Riposte is also down, catch her with Nasus W Wither and start the fight.
Fiora.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. After Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora W Riposte are down, catch her with Nasus W Wither for a short trade, and don’t chase her recklessly. In a small skirmish, you can wait until after Fiora goes in to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands.
Fiora.laning: If Fiora pushes the lane, let it come to you and farm near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire, since it pushes the lane and uses mana. If Fiora’s pressure makes even last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Fiora.phase: Nasus gets stronger in the mid to late game as you build stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands.
Fiora.teamfight: Don’t go in first alone; engage after your team starts the fight. If Fiora targets your back line, catch her with Nasus W Wither and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stay near a wall so she can’t reach all four vitals.
Fiora.watch: Watch the direction of Fiora P Duelist’s Dance’s vital and stand on the opposite side, then counterattack when Fiora closes in with Fiora Q Lunge. Don’t rush Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while Fiora W Riposte is ready, and move to the side as you attack to avoid Riposte. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stay near a wall so she can’t reach all four vitals.

Gangplank.build: Gangplank Q Parrrley harasses hard, so prioritize armor from the laning phase onward. Get health to prepare for the true damage, and if the healing from Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is a problem, fit in Executioner's Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Gangplank.combo: After Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold him on the ground effect with Nasus W Wither, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Gangplank.escape: Go in right after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, while it’s still unprimed, and Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down. Gangplank has no ability to create distance on his own, so use this chance to hold him with Nasus W Wither.
Gangplank.fight: Try to trade right after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, before the keg is primed. Back off if there’s a primed keg nearby, and fight after Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, holding him with Nasus W Wither.
Gangplank.laning: Early on, don’t force the wave forward; farm last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire under your turret. If Gangplank Q Parrrley pressure makes even last hitting difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Gangplank.phase: Nasus gets strong in the mid to late game with stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, but simply waiting won’t put you ahead if you’re being kept from farming and can’t build stacks.
Gangplank.teamfight: Don’t go in first on your own; engage after your allies initiate, and avoid the blast radius of primed Gangplank E Powder Keg. Cast Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Gangplank.watch: When Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed, its explosion and slow are dangerous, so destroy it from outside its range and don’t step where two kegs overlap.

Garen.build: Build armor first to prepare for the physical damage from Garen Q Decisive Strike and Garen E Judgment, and get health to prepare for Garen R Demacian Justice. Fit in Dead Man's Plate for survival, and if the healing from Garen P Perseverance is a problem, add Executioner's Calling.
Garen.combo: After the silence from Garen Q Decisive Strike has ended and Garen W Courage’s brief shield and tenacity window has passed, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold him with W so he stays on E, then land Q after E reduces his armor.
Garen.escape: The window to go in is right after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack is consumed. Garen has no ability to create distance on his own, so hold him with Nasus W Wither then, but delay your combo by half a beat right after he activates Garen W Courage.
Garen.fight: Early on, avoid extended fights and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Trade briefly after Garen Q Decisive Strike is used on a minion or its empowered attack is consumed, and move out of range while Garen E Judgment is spinning.
Garen.laning: If Garen pushes the lane, let the wave come in and farm last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire here, since it pushes the wave and can make you miss last hits. If his pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Garen.phase: Nasus gets strong in the mid to late game with stacks and access to Nasus R Fury of the Sands, but Garen also retains the stats he has built with Garen W Courage, so don’t miss out on farming.
Garen.teamfight: Don’t engage first on your own; go in after your allies start the fight. Cast Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry or a target diving your backline, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they’re on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Garen.watch: If you approach while Garen Q Decisive Strike is active, its silence makes it hard to fight back. Don’t stay long in the spin range of Garen E Judgment, and if your health drops below half, move out of Garen R Demacian Justice’s range to avoid it.

Gnar.build: Build armor first against the main sources of Gnar’s damage: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss, Gnar E Hop / Crunch, and Gnar R GNAR!. Gnar W Hyper / Wallop deals magic damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about building a lot of health alone. Fit in at least one survival item, and consider tenacity against Mega Gnar’s wall stun.
Gnar.combo: When engaging, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Gnar on E with W, then land Q after E reduces his armor. In a skirmish, you can also activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Gnar goes in.
Gnar.escape: Right after Mega Gnar turns back into Mini Gnar, he can’t transform again for a while, creating an opportunity to go in. Close the distance right after making him use Gnar E Hop / Crunch as well. Don’t go in first when Gnar R GNAR! can stun you against a wall.
Gnar.fight: Early on, avoid forced fights while taking Gnar’s ranged harass. Right after Mega Gnar turns back into Mini Gnar or right after Gnar uses E Hop / Crunch, hold him in place with Nasus W Wither and approach. Back off and wait out the time right after he transforms into Mega Gnar.
Gnar.laning: Don’t force the wave forward; build stacks by farming last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire during this phase to reduce the chance of pushing the wave and missing Q last hits. If Gnar’s pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Gnar.phase: In the mid game, look for fights when your stacks are built and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is ready, and back off right after Gnar transforms into Mega Gnar. In the late game, use your Q stacks to choose between a front-to-front fight and split pressure on a turret.
Gnar.teamfight: Check your position first, since fighting with your back to a wall or in narrow terrain increases the risk of being stunned by Gnar R GNAR!. After your allies engage, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and go in. Cast Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then use Q while they’re on E. If Gnar targets your backline, cast W on him to hold him in place.
Gnar.watch: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss slows, and Mini Gnar’s boomerang can hit you on its return as well. Step out of its path so Gnar can’t catch it again. Mega Gnar’s Gnar R GNAR! stuns enemies who hit a wall, so avoid fighting with your back to a wall or in narrow terrain.

Gwen.build: Build magic resistance first against Gwen’s main damage, and get armor as well to help against her basic attacks. Avoid building a lot of health alone, since she deals damage based on your maximum health.
Gwen.combo: If Gwen W Hallowed Mist prevents you from targeting her with Nasus W Wither, enter the mist or wait for it to end. In a fight, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Gwen on E with W, reduce her armor with E, then land Q.
Gwen.escape: Right after making Gwen use E Skip 'n Slash is a window for Nasus to go in. However, if Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, check that you’re in a position where you can cast Nasus W Wither before going in. Move to the side so you don’t stand in the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!.
Gwen.fight: Right after Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is a chance to close the distance. Cast Nasus W Wither after Gwen W Hallowed Mist ends or once you’re inside the mist. Fight while avoiding the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!.
Gwen.laning: If Gwen pushes the lane, let the wave come in and farm last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire; save mana for fights and following up on ganks. If Gwen’s pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Gwen.phase: From the mid game onward, Nasus gets much stronger as he builds stacks and gains access to Nasus R Fury of the Sands. In the late game, use your accumulated stacks to fight or pressure a split push by quickly hitting turrets with Q.
Gwen.teamfight: Don’t engage first on your own; go in after your allies initiate. If Gwen targets your backline, hold her with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while she’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Avoid the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip! while dealing area damage with Nasus R Fury of the Sands and continuing to land Q.
Gwen.watch: The center of the cone of Gwen Q Snip Snip! deals true damage, so move to the side when she casts it to avoid the center. While Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, you can’t target her with Nasus W Wither from outside the mist, so enter the mist or wait until it ends.

Illaoi.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God, Q Tentacle Smash, and W Harsh Lesson. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building a lot of health alone.
Illaoi.combo: In a fight, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W’s slow to keep Illaoi on E, reduce her armor with E, then land Q. If you bought Executioner's Calling, also apply Grievous Wounds with a Q hit.
Illaoi.escape: After dodging Illaoi E Test of Spirit, close the distance right after she uses W Harsh Lesson. Slow her with Nasus W Wither and fight away from the tentacles. If you have no intention of fighting but your spirit is pulled, break the tether, dodge the first tentacle, then wait beside it until the mark ends.
Illaoi.fight: Early on, avoid direct fights and build Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks. Dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit, make her use W Harsh Lesson, then fight away from the tentacles. Even if your spirit is pulled, fight back instead of just running if the situation allows it.
Illaoi.laning: If Illaoi pushes the lane, let the wave come in near your turret and farm last hits with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Avoid tentacles near walls and look for last hits from outside Illaoi E Test of Spirit’s range. Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire under your turret, and if you can’t even last hit, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Illaoi.phase: From the mid game onward, Nasus gets strong when he has built stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands. In the late game, use your accumulated stacks to fight or apply split pressure by quickly hitting turrets with Q.
Illaoi.teamfight: If you group in front of Illaoi, Illaoi R Leap of Faith creates more tentacles, so spread out and back away while her ultimate is active. If you can’t destroy the tentacles, pull Illaoi into open ground away from walls. After your allies start the fight, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and go in. Cast W Wither on a threatening enemy, then use Q Siphoning Strike while they’re on E Spirit Fire.
Illaoi.watch: Illaoi E Test of Spirit slows and marks you, so last hit from outside its range and avoid it. When Illaoi uses R Leap of Faith, don’t group up; back away from the tentacles and wait out its duration.

Irelia.build: Build armor first against Irelia’s main damage from Irelia Q Bladesurge and Irelia W Defiant Dance. If the healing from Irelia Q Bladesurge is a problem, fit in Executioner's Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Even if you invest in offense, include a survival item such as Dead Man's Plate.
Irelia.combo: When Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Irelia on Nasus E Spirit Fire with Nasus W Wither, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after her armor is reduced.
Irelia.escape: Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down is a chance to approach. If you’ve also dodged Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun, hold Irelia in place with Nasus W Wither and fight.
Irelia.fight: Approach after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, then use Nasus W Wither to reduce her movement and attack speed. In a skirmish, look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Irelia goes in.
Irelia.laning: If Irelia pushes the lane, let the wave come in and focus on last hitting near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire; save mana for fights or jungle help. If Irelia pressures too hard for you to build stacks, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Irelia.phase: Nasus gets strong from the mid to late game as he builds stacks and gains access to Nasus R Fury of the Sands. In the late game, use your accumulated stacks to fight or pressure turrets with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Irelia.teamfight: Irelia R Vanguard's Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet have a big impact in teamfights, so focus on pressuring Irelia. Rather than going in first on your own, enter after your allies start the fight, cast Nasus W Wither on Irelia, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while she’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Also hold her with Nasus W Wither when she targets your backline.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain through low-health minions to approach, so create distance when minions are close to dying. Avoid the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and if you’re trapped by Irelia R Vanguard's Edge, wait until the blades disappear.

Jax.build: Prioritize defensive items like Dead Man's Plate. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so don’t focus on only one resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on your max health, so be wary of stacking health alone.
Jax.combo: After Jax E Counter Strike is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Jax in the area with Nasus W Wither, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then hit him with the empowered basic attack from Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Jax.escape: The window to engage is after Jax E Counter Strike’s stun is down. If Jax Q Leap Strike has just been used too, he’ll have a hard time creating distance again, so apply Nasus W Wither and try to fight.
Jax.fight: Avoid direct fights early and stack Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. After Jax E Counter Strike ends, fight while slowing his movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither. In skirmishes, if Jax goes in, you can also choose to delay activating Nasus R Fury of the Sands.
Jax.laning: When the wave pushes toward you, farm with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret and don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire. If you can’t even last-hit, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Jax.phase: Nasus is weak early, so prioritize stacking Nasus Q Siphoning Strike over trading. With consistent stacking, Nasus gains more of an advantage as the game goes late and can choose between teamfights and side-lane pressure.
Jax.teamfight: If Jax jumps in with Jax E Counter Strike active, don’t group around him; wait until the AoE stun ends. Enter after your allies start the fight, then use Nasus W Wither to cripple Jax or the enemy carry’s movement and attack speed, and land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. When Jax pushes turrets in a side lane, look for an objective trade instead of forcing a one-on-one.
Jax.watch: Jax Q Leap Strike can close the gap, so don’t force a fight until Jax E Counter Strike ends.

Jayce.build: Build magic resistance first against Jayce W Lightning Field / Hyper Charge and Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate. Also account for the physical damage from Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast, and get movement speed to leave telegraphed attack areas, plus a survival item such as Dead Man's Plate. Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building a lot of health alone.
Jayce.combo: After the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Hold Jayce on the ground effect with Nasus W Wither, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land an empowered basic attack.
Jayce.escape: Right after the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! is down is a chance for Nasus to close the distance. If Jayce is in hammer form, watch for the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow as well, and go in with Nasus W Wither after that ability is down.
Jayce.fight: Early on, withstand Jayce’s harass and farm last hits with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. After the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, close the distance, hold him with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. In a skirmish, you can also activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Jayce goes in.
Jayce.laning: Jayce Q Shock Blast travels in a straight line, so move side to side while farming, and dodge immediately to the side when you see Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If Jayce pushes the lane, don’t force the wave forward; farm last hits near your turret with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike and preserve mana. Don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire during that phase, and if his pressure makes even last hitting difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Jayce.phase: In the mid game, build Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks and look for chances to fight when you can activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands. If you survive the early game and build stacks, Nasus has the advantage as the game goes late.
Jayce.teamfight: Nasus doesn’t go in first on his own; he enters after his allies start the fight. If the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, hold Jayce with Nasus W Wither and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands to deal area damage and make use of the reduced cooldown on Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Jayce.watch: When Jayce has his cannon, watch for ranged harass. If you see Jayce E Acceleration Gate, step sideways out of the straight line where Jayce Q Shock Blast will travel. When he has his hammer, watch for the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! and the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow.

Malphite.build: Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Malphite Q Seismic Shard, E Ground Slam, and R Unstoppable Force. Reduce Malphite’s high armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, and include at least one defensive item like Dead Man's Plate even if you focus on damage.
Malphite.combo: After breaking Malphite P Granite Shield, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Malphite in the Nasus E Spirit Fire area with W, reduce his armor with E, then land Q.
Malphite.escape: After Malphite goes in with R, you can slow him with Nasus W Wither and fight back, but W can’t interrupt the dash itself.
Malphite.fight: Break Malphite P Granite Shield first, and avoid trading damage right after Malphite Q Seismic Shard hits you. In short trades, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Malphite goes in, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Malphite.laning: Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire here; save mana for gank follow-up or fights. If you can’t even last-hit with Q, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Malphite.phase: Nasus grows strong in the mid-to-late game with stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, but against Malphite’s increased armor, place Nasus E Spirit Fire first before fighting.
Malphite.teamfight: Spread out so Malphite R Unstoppable Force doesn’t knock up several allies, and counterattack right after his R is down. Enter after your allies start the fight, apply Nasus W Wither to the enemy carry, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Malphite.watch: Malphite Q Seismic Shard slows you, making it hard to engage or disengage, so don’t start a trade right after it hits. Malphite R Unstoppable Force is an unstoppable dash that knocks up multiple targets, so don’t group with allies when you can’t see where he is, and avoid giving him an engage angle.

Olaf.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Olaf Q Undertow. Olaf E Reckless Swing deals true damage that resistances can’t reduce, so build health too. Include at least one defensive item like Dead Man's Plate even if you focus on damage.
Olaf.combo: After Olaf R Ragnarok ends, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Olaf in E’s area with W, let E reduce his armor, then land Q.
Olaf.escape: Create distance while Olaf R Ragnarok is active, and use the moment it ends as an opening to engage with Nasus W Wither. Moving opposite the axe from Olaf Q Undertow so he can’t retrieve it makes it harder for him to poke and approach. Olaf has no ability to create distance on his own, so if you have a chance to catch him, keep chasing with W.
Olaf.fight: Avoid direct fights early; stack Nasus Q Siphoning Strike before fighting. After Olaf R Ragnarok ends, slow his movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. Olaf gains attack speed and healing as his health drops, so don’t recklessly engage just because he’s at half health.
Olaf.laning: Don’t push the wave with Nasus E Spirit Fire here; save mana for fights and gank follow-up. If Olaf’s pressure makes it hard to last-hit with Q, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Olaf.phase: From mid game onward, once Nasus has stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, look for opportunities to fight. The later the game goes, the more favorable it becomes for Nasus, so use your stacks to fight or pressure turrets.
Olaf.teamfight: Don’t engage first on your own; go in after your allies start the fight. If Olaf R Ragnarok is active, create distance and let it run out, then use Nasus W Wither to catch Olaf if he’s targeting an ally. Use Q in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire, then activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands to use its AoE damage and reduced Q cooldown.
Olaf.watch: Olaf Q Undertow reduces your armor and slows you, so move opposite the direction where the axe lands to prevent him from picking it up. Olaf E Reckless Swing deals true damage, so relying on armor alone when your health is low is dangerous. While Olaf R Ragnarok is active, don’t try to catch him with Nasus W Wither; create distance and apply it after R ends.

Ornn.build: Ornn deals both physical and magic damage, so don't build only one type of resistance. Ornn W Bellows Breath deals damage based on your maximum health and can lead into crowd control, so you can prioritize tenacity. Even if you focus on damage, include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man's Plate.
Ornn.combo: In trades, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Ornn on E with W, then hit him with Q after E reduces his armor.
Ornn.escape: Don't engage just because Ornn E Searing Charge is down. Your chance comes after Ornn R Call of the Forge God is down too; then hold him with Nasus W Wither. If Ornn W Bellows Breath makes you Brittle, delay your engage until it wears off.
Ornn.fight: Early on, focus on stacking with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike instead of taking direct fights. If Ornn E Searing Charge is down and Ornn R Call of the Forge God is also unavailable, use Nasus W Wither to hold him and fight. If Ornn engages first in a skirmish, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and fight back.
Ornn.laning: Don't push the lane recklessly; let it come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Near your turret, don't use Nasus E Spirit Fire, since it pushes the wave and can make you miss Q last hits. If Ornn tries to forge an item in lane, stay close and attack to interrupt him.
Ornn.phase: Nasus gets stronger from mid game onward with his stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Use your stacks in the late game, but apply pressure before Ornn's items and his allies' Masterwork upgrades build up.
Ornn.teamfight: Don't lead the engage alone; go in after your team starts the fight. Dodge the spirit from Ornn R Call of the Forge God by moving sideways, and get out of the straight line where Ornn can knock it back. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they are on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Ornn.watch: Stand away from the pillar created by Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture and from walls. Ornn E Searing Charge knocks you up if it hits a pillar or wall, so move toward open space when you see him prepare it. If you are hit by the final breath of Ornn W Bellows Breath, keep your distance until Brittle wears off.

Pantheon.build: Build armor first against Pantheon's main damage. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a lot of health. Pantheon R Grand Starfall has armor penetration, so mix in defensive items such as Dead Man's Plate instead of stacking only armor.
Pantheon.combo: Keep Pantheon's stun and frontal defense in mind, and use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither to hold Pantheon on the area, then reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire before landing Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, wait for it to end or attack from the side.
Pantheon.escape: Once Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, you can engage without worrying about its stun. Look for an opening before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back, and wait until Pantheon E Aegis Assault has also ended before holding him with Nasus W Wither. If only one of Pantheon's mobility abilities is down, he can escape by another means, so don't overextend to chase him.
Pantheon.fight: Avoid early trades and fight after building stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If Pantheon engages in a skirmish, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands, use Nasus W Wither to hold him, and attack while he is on Nasus E Spirit Fire. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault is blocking the front, save Nasus Q Siphoning Strike and wait for it to end.
Pantheon.laning: Don't fight Pantheon head-on early. If the wave pushes toward you, last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret. Near your turret, don't use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave; save mana for fights and gank follow-up. Stand behind minions against Pantheon Q Comet Spear, and if even last-hitting is difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Pantheon.phase: In the mid game, build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike and look for fights when Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available. Nasus gets stronger in the late game while Pantheon's influence falls off, so use your stacks to fight or push the lane and pressure turrets.
Pantheon.teamfight: Don't lead the engage alone; go in after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on enemies targeting your back line, including Pantheon, or on the enemy carry, then attack with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in the area of Nasus E Spirit Fire. When Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, it deals continuous damage nearby and lets you use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike repeatedly.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault is a targeted stun, so be careful not to let him get in range to dash to you. You can reduce the damage from Pantheon Q Comet Spear by keeping minions between you and him. When Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, don't attack him from the front; wait for it to end or reposition to his side. If you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of its area.

Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy Q Hammer Shock, E Heroic Charge, and R Keeper's Verdict. Even if you focus on damage, get at least one defensive item such as Dead Man's Plate.
Poppy.combo: In trades, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W's slow to keep Poppy on E, then hit her with Q after E reduces her armor.
Poppy.escape: The moment Poppy E Heroic Charge is down is your chance to close the distance. If you see her charging Poppy R Keeper's Verdict, first sidestep away from directly in front of her to avoid being displaced. Nasus has no ability to escape on his own, so don't engage with a wall behind you.
Poppy.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Once Poppy E Heroic Charge is down, close the distance in open space and trade while slowing her with Nasus W Wither. In skirmishes, look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Poppy engages.
Poppy.laning: If Poppy pushes the wave, farm it near your turret and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire, since it pushes the wave and costs mana. If her pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap.
Poppy.phase: Nasus gets stronger in the mid to late game as his Q stacks build and Nasus R Fury of the Sands becomes available. In the late game, use your stacks to fight or split-push and pressure turrets.
Poppy.teamfight: Don't lead the engage alone; go in after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then hit them with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they are on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Once the team fight starts, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands to deal area damage and use Q repeatedly.
Poppy.watch: Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns if it knocks you into a wall, so stand in open space with no wall behind you. If Poppy Q Hammer Shock hits you, immediately leave the remaining zone to avoid its second hit. When Poppy spins her hammer and charges R Keeper's Verdict, sidestep away from directly in front of her.

Renekton.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Renekton Q Cull the Meek, W Ruthless Predator, and E Slice and Dice. If Renekton Q Cull the Meek's healing is a problem, fit in Executioner's Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Against the armor reduction from Renekton E Slice and Dice, position to avoid the dash instead of just stacking more armor.
Renekton.combo: In trades, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither to keep Renekton on the area, then reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire before landing Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Renekton.escape: The moment Renekton E Slice and Dice is used to disengage is your chance to close the distance. If Renekton W Ruthless Predator is also down and his Fury bar is empty, hold him with Nasus W Wither and counterattack.
Renekton.fight: Look to trade when Renekton's Fury bar is empty. If you survive his first combo of Renekton Q Cull the Meek, W Ruthless Predator, and E Slice and Dice, counterattack after his abilities are down. When you go in, hold him with Nasus W Wither and hit him with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he is on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Renekton.laning: Avoid direct fights early and build last hits with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If Renekton pushes the wave, farm it near your turret and don't use Nasus E Spirit Fire there. If his pressure makes even Nasus Q Siphoning Strike last hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Renekton.phase: After mid game, Renekton's value falls off and Nasus becomes strong as his stacks build. In the late game, look for direct fights with Nasus R Fury of the Sands active or pressure turrets with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Renekton.teamfight: Don't lead the engage; go in after your team starts the fight. Activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands, hold the enemy carry with Nasus W Wither, then hit them with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they are on Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Renekton targets your back line, hold him with Nasus W Wither.
Renekton.watch: If Renekton's Fury bar is over half full or just below half because of Renekton P Reign of Anger, watch out for the empowered stun from Renekton W Ruthless Predator and stay out of range. Renekton E Slice and Dice unlocks a second dash if the first hits a unit, so don't stand in or behind a minion wave.

Riven.build: Riven deals physical damage, so build armor first. If Riven gets ahead, buy defensive items sooner. Include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man's Plate so you can survive focused attacks even with Nasus R Fury of the Sands active, and get health to prepare for Riven R Blade of the Exile.
Riven.combo: Right after Riven gets close, use Nasus W Wither, then place Nasus E Spirit Fire and land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither's slow to keep Riven on the area, then reduce her armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire before hitting her with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Riven.escape: Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven E Valor are both mobility abilities, so don't chase when only one is down. Go in when Riven Q Broken Wings has been used to clear minions and Riven E Valor is also down. Checking whether Riven W Ki Burst is down can also reduce the risk of being stunned.
Riven.fight: Avoid direct fights early, and look to trade when Riven Q Broken Wings is used to clear minions. If Riven gets close, use Nasus W Wither to reduce her movement and attack speed, then hit her with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while she is on Nasus E Spirit Fire. In skirmishes, it's better to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Riven engages.
Riven.laning: During this phase, don't use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave; save mana for fights. If Riven's pressure makes even Nasus Q Siphoning Strike last hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Riven.phase: From mid game onward, fights get stronger as your stacks build and Nasus R Fury of the Sands becomes available. In the late game, use your stacks to fight or split-push and pressure turrets with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Riven.teamfight: Don't go in first; engage after your team starts the fight. If Riven dives your back line, use Nasus W Wither to reduce her movement and attack speed, then hit her with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while she is on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Keep Riven's dashes and stun in mind as you activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike repeatedly.
Riven.watch: Riven uses Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven E Valor for chained dashes, so when you see the first dash, back away to create distance. The third cast of Riven Q Broken Wings knocks you up, and Riven W Ki Burst stuns, so once she catches you, her follow-up is hard to avoid. When Riven R Blade of the Exile is active, her range increases and its finisher deals damage based on your missing health, so keep your distance until it expires.

Rumble.build: Rumble P Junkyard Titan and Rumble Q Flamespitter deal damage based on your maximum health, so avoid a defensive build that only adds health. Prioritize defensive items with magic resistance, and keep in mind that Rumble E Electro Harpoon reduces that resistance if it hits you.
Rumble.combo: After Rumble W Scrap Shield's shield disappears, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W to keep Rumble on E, then hit him with Q after E's armor reduction takes effect.
Rumble.escape: Look for an engage after Rumble uses W Scrap Shield and you have waited out its shield. Create distance before the second shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon hits, and hold Rumble with Nasus W Wither when you won't be caught by the harpoon's slow. Rumble has no mobility ability, so once you catch him, his escape options are limited.
Rumble.fight: Early on, avoid fights that leave you exposed to Rumble Q Flamespitter for a long time, and fight at a distance where Rumble has to walk forward. Build stacks, briefly wait out Rumble W Scrap Shield, then hold him with Nasus W Wither and fight. In skirmishes, you can also activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Rumble engages.
Rumble.laning: Early on, don't push the lane recklessly; let it come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Near your turret, protect the wave and your Q last hits by not using Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Rumble's pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Rumble.phase: Nasus gets stronger from the mid to late game as his stacks build and Nasus R Fury of the Sands becomes available. If you're kept from farming early, you won't get stronger as the game goes on, so ask for help.
Rumble.teamfight: Don't go in first; engage after your team starts the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then hit them with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they are on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Watch your distance so Rumble E Electro Harpoon's slow doesn't leave you exposed to Rumble Q Flamespitter for too long.
Rumble.watch: If the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon hits you, immediately create distance. Be careful not to get caught by the slow from Rumble R The Equalizer.

Sett.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Sett P Pit Grit and Sett Q Knuckle Down. Sett Q Knuckle Down deals damage based on your maximum health, and resistance does not work against the center of Sett W Haymaker’s true damage, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone. Even if you build mostly damage, include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man’s Plate.
Sett.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Sett on E with W, then land Q after his armor is reduced. Immediately after dealing damage, make sure you have enough distance to dodge Sett W Haymaker.
Sett.escape: If Sett E Facebreaker is also down, start a fight with Nasus W Wither during the window when the risk of being grabbed is lower.
Sett.fight: Once you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available, if Sett E Facebreaker or Sett R The Show Stopper is down, close in with Nasus W Wither to reduce Sett’s movement speed and attack speed. After dealing damage, briefly create distance to watch for Sett W Haymaker, which grows stronger as he takes damage.
Sett.laning: If Sett pushes the lane, collect the wave near your turret and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Don’t push the lane with Nasus E Spirit Fire; save mana for fights or jungle assistance. If Sett’s pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Sett.phase: From mid game onward, once you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available, you become much stronger in fights. In the late game, fight with your accumulated stacks or push a side lane alone to pressure a turret.
Sett.teamfight: Don’t go in first by yourself; enter after your allies start the fight. If Sett goes after your back line, use Nasus W Wither to reduce his movement speed and attack speed, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. If you have dealt enough damage to strengthen Sett W Haymaker, move out of the center of its aim.
Sett.watch: Sett E Facebreaker stuns when there is an enemy on each side of Sett, so position yourself to avoid getting caught between a minion wave and Sett. Sett W Haymaker gets stronger after he takes damage, so create some distance after trading. If it is hard to dodge, move to the side of the center of its aim to avoid the true damage. Sett R The Show Stopper suppresses you if it grabs you, and Flash or Cleanse cannot break it, so stay wary of its grab range while Sett has R available.

Shen.build: Prioritize tenacity against the taunt from Shen E Shadow Dash. Shen E Shadow Dash deals physical damage and Shen Q Twilight Assault deals magic damage, so don't focus on only one type of resistance. Include at least one defensive item, but avoid choices that only add health since Shen Q Twilight Assault deals damage based on your maximum health.
Shen.combo: After Shen E Shadow Dash misses, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither to keep Shen on the area and reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire before attacking. If Shen W Spirit's Refuge is active, wait until it ends before using Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Shen.escape: The moment Shen E Shadow Dash misses is your chance to counterattack. However, if Shen R Stand United is still available, he can escape, so look for an opening before Shen R Stand United becomes available again.
Shen.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If Shen E Shadow Dash misses, hold him with Nasus W Wither and fight. If Shen W Spirit's Refuge is active, your basic attacks are blocked, so use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after it ends.
Shen.laning: If Shen pushes the lane, last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret. Save mana by not using Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave and risk missing last hits. If Shen leaves the lane with Shen R Stand United, gain an advantage by pressuring turrets on that side.
Shen.phase: From the mid to late game, direct fights become favorable once your stacks build and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available. In the late game, use your stacks to fight or pressure turrets.
Shen.teamfight: Shen can join fights in other lanes with Shen R Stand United, so alert your team if Shen disappears or starts channeling. Engage after your team starts the fight, use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while they are on Nasus E Spirit Fire. If Shen targets your back line, hold him with Nasus W Wither.
Shen.watch: If taunted by Shen E Shadow Dash, you will take empowered basic attacks from Shen Q Twilight Assault, so dodge the dash. Also move out of the path of Shen Q Twilight Assault's returning spirit blade, and save Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while Shen W Spirit's Refuge is active.

Singed.build: Against this opponent, prioritize movement speed and magic resistance. Singed’s main damage is magic damage, and it’s important to walk out of the telegraphed Singed Q Poison Trail. Singed E Fling deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone.
Singed.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Singed on E with W, then hit Q after E’s armor reduction applies. Don’t chase recklessly through Singed Q Poison Trail just to continue the combo.
Singed.escape: After Singed uses Singed W Mega Adhesive and Singed E Fling, you have a chance to catch him. Singed has no skill that creates distance on his own, so close in while slowing him with Nasus W Wither. If the adhesive is still on the ground, go around it, and stop chasing through his poison.
Singed.fight: Early on, prioritize last-hitting with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike and avoid risky head-on fights. If Singed comes within grab range, slow him with Nasus W Wither and hit Q on Nasus E Spirit Fire. If you would have to follow Singed Q Poison Trail to chase him, stop pursuing.
Singed.laning: If Singed pushes the lane, collect the wave near your turret and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Nasus E Spirit Fire pushes the lane and uses a lot of mana, so save it for fights or to follow up on a gank. If Singed’s pressure makes even Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Singed.phase: Even if you have an early opportunity, focus on building Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks instead of taking a risky fight. Nasus becomes strong in the mid to late game once you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available, so fight using those stacks or pressure a turret.
Singed.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies start the fight. If Singed dives onto your allies, hold him with Nasus W Wither and use that opening to attack his teammates rather than chasing him all the way. In fights, hit Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire and make use of successive Q attacks during Nasus R Fury of the Sands.
Singed.watch: Don’t chase Singed, even when his health is low. You’ll have to run through Singed Q Poison Trail, and if Singed R Insanity Potion is active, healing is also reduced. Go around areas covered by Singed W Mega Adhesive, and check behind Singed so Singed E Fling doesn’t toss you into the enemy team.

Sion.build: Build armor first against Sion P Glory in Death, Sion Q Decimating Smash, and Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught, his main sources of damage. Sion E Roar of the Slayer reduces armor, so prioritize avoiding it, and include at least one defensive item.
Sion.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Sion on the area with the slow, then land an empowered basic attack after his armor is reduced. If Sion W Soul Furnace was just activated, focus your damage before the shield bursts.
Sion.escape: The chance to go in comes after Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught, his mobility ability, is down.
Sion.fight: Avoid head-on fights early and fight after building Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks. When you dodge Sion Q Decimating Smash to the side or Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught is down, catch Sion with Nasus W Wither and trade. In small skirmishes, look for a chance to activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Sion goes in.
Sion.laning: If Sion pushes the lane, collect the wave near your turret and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Save Nasus E Spirit Fire, since it pushes the lane and uses a lot of mana. If Sion’s pressure makes even last-hitting difficult, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Sion.phase: From mid game onward, your stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands make you strong in head-on fights. In the late game, you can pressure turrets by split pushing, but Sion’s maximum health also grows as he farms, so don’t let him farm freely for too long.
Sion.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies start the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Reposition to avoid attacks from Sion P Glory in Death where Sion falls.
Sion.watch: Sion Q Decimating Smash knocks you up and stuns you if charged for a long time, so move to the side when you see it charging. Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught travels almost in a straight line, so avoid narrow paths and sidestep it. After Sion falls, Sion P Glory in Death revives him and lets him attack quickly, so reposition.

Teemo.build: Teemo’s main damage comes from the magic damage of Teemo Q Blinding Dart, Teemo E Toxic Shot, and Teemo R Noxious Trap, so build magic resistance first. Even if you build mostly attack damage, include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man’s Plate.
Teemo.combo: When Teemo Q Blinding Dart is down and you can close in, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Keep Teemo on the area with Nasus W Wither, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Teemo.escape: The chance to go in comes right after Teemo Q Blinding Dart is down. Don’t chase recklessly while Teemo uses Teemo W Move Quick to create distance; catch him with Nasus W Wither when you can close the gap.
Teemo.fight: Early on, avoid short trades where you take a few hits and back off. Right after Teemo Q Blinding Dart is down, close the gap with Nasus W Wither, and once you’re on him, keep fighting. While blinded, use Nasus E Spirit Fire instead of basic attacks or back off.
Teemo.laning: Early on, don’t push the lane aggressively; let it come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Near your turret, don’t push the lane with Nasus E Spirit Fire, and save mana. If Teemo’s pressure makes even last hits difficult, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Teemo.phase: From mid game onward, you get stronger once you have stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available, and if you survive the early game, things get more favorable as the game goes on. If you can’t farm and build stacks, you won’t get stronger over time.
Teemo.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies start the fight. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy’s main damage dealer, then hit Nasus Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Use Oracle Lens to clear Teemo R Noxious Trap around objectives and in narrow passages before moving through.
Teemo.watch: Teemo Q Blinding Dart blocks basic attacks, so don’t try to hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while blinded. Teemo E Toxic Shot applies poison damage even after a single basic attack, so stay out of range if you aren’t ready to commit. Also watch for Teemo P Guerrilla Warfare in brush and Teemo R Noxious Trap in choke points.

Trundle.build: Build armor first against Trundle Q Chomp and his basic attacks. However, Trundle R Subjugate deals magic damage and reduces resistances, so prioritize getting out of its range over stacking more resistances. If the healing from Trundle P King’s Tribute is a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Trundle.combo: When fighting outside Trundle W Frozen Domain, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Slow Trundle with W to keep him on E, then land Q after E’s armor reduction applies.
Trundle.escape: Go in after Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down and you’re out of Trundle W Frozen Domain. If you catch Trundle with Nasus W Wither, he has no skill to create distance on his own, so it’s hard for him to get away. If the pillar blocks you instead, move to the side immediately instead of continuing the fight.
Trundle.fight: Early on, avoid head-on trades and build Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks. When fighting, back out of Trundle W Frozen Domain, then go back in, and reduce Trundle’s movement speed and attack speed with Nasus W Wither. Create distance while Trundle R Subjugate is active, then fight again afterward.
Trundle.teamfight: Don’t go in first; enter after your allies start the fight. If Trundle goes after your back line, reduce his movement speed and attack speed with Nasus W Wither, then use Q Siphoning Strike on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Trundle.watch: Trundle W Frozen Domain increases his attack speed, movement speed, and healing received, so don’t fight inside it; back off and wait out its duration. Trundle E Pillar of Ice blocks escape routes in narrow paths, so fight in open terrain and move to the side immediately when the pillar appears. While Trundle R Subjugate is active, you take damage based on your maximum health and lose resistances, so create distance.

Udyr.build: Build armor first to prepare for Udyr’s basic attacks and Udyr Q Wilding Claw. If the magic damage from Udyr R Wingborne Storm is a problem, build some magic resistance too, and avoid stacking health alone. If the healing from Udyr W Iron Mantle is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling.
Udyr.combo: After Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield is gone, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Slow Udyr’s movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after Nasus E Spirit Fire reduces his armor.
Udyr.escape: The moment after you make Udyr use Udyr E Blazing Stampede is your window to close the distance and go in. After you’ve taken one stun, use the period when Udyr cannot stun you again with it to counterattack or retreat.
Udyr.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Engage when Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield is gone or right after Udyr uses Udyr E Blazing Stampede. In small skirmishes, activating Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Udyr goes in is a good option.
Udyr.laning: Udyr can show up from the jungle to gank, so place vision at key routes and jungle entrances, and don’t push the lane and move up when he’s out of sight.
