Let the wave come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike; don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire near your turret. If Udyr’s pressure makes it hard to last-hit at all, ask for jungle assistance or a lane swap.
Udyr.phase: In the mid and late game, your stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands make you strong in direct fights. Later on, join teamfights or pressure turrets with your accumulated stacks.
Udyr.teamfight: Don’t go in alone; wait for your team to engage, then activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands and join the fight. Don’t fixate on Udyr while he survives with defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle; use Nasus W Wither to catch the enemy carry or an enemy diving your backline. Land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while the target is on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Udyr.watch: Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s fast dash and stun are dangerous, so don’t move forward when Udyr is out of sight. Udyr Q Wilding Claw and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deal damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on your health alone to stand your ground.

Urgot.build: Build armor first since Urgot’s main damage is physical. Even if you focus on damage, include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man’s Plate.
Urgot.combo: After Urgot E Disdain is down, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither to keep Urgot in the area, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after his armor is reduced.
Urgot.escape: Urgot E Disdain is his only mobility tool, so the moment after he uses it is your chance to engage. On the other hand, if Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits you or Urgot E Disdain is still available, keep your distance first since Nasus has no skill to escape.
Urgot.fight: Avoid direct fights early, and only close the distance right after Urgot uses Urgot E Disdain. If Urgot approaches with Urgot W Purge active, don’t rely on the slow from Nasus W Wither alone; walk out of his range. When you fight, reduce his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Urgot.laning: If Urgot pushes the lane, let the wave come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret. Don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave; save mana for fights and gank follow-ups. If Urgot’s pressure makes it hard to last-hit at all, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Urgot.phase: From the mid game onward, opportunities to fight increase when you can use your Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks and Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Later on, fight with your accumulated stacks or pressure turrets with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Urgot.teamfight: Don’t go in alone; wait until your team starts the fight, then engage. Urgot E Disdain stops at the first champion it hits, so stand with your frontline to keep your allies behind you from getting caught. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while the target is on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Urgot.watch: Urgot P Echoing Flames deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t stay near him for long. Urgot Q Corrosive Charge slows you and lets Urgot W Purge focus its shots on you, so dodge the charge and keep your distance. If Urgot R Fear Beyond Death hits you, get completely out of Urgot’s range before you reach the execution threshold.

Volibear.build: Build armor first to prepare for the physical damage from Volibear Q Thundering Smash, Volibear W Frenzied Maul, and Volibear R Stormbringer. If the healing from Volibear W Frenzied Maul is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Volibear.combo: Use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use W to hold Volibear in E’s area, then land Q after E’s armor reduction applies.
Volibear.escape: Even if you dodge the stun from Volibear Q Thundering Smash, don’t go in right away if Volibear R Stormbringer is still available. Look to engage after both mobility tools are down and before R comes back, when the stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm have also fallen off.
Volibear.fight: Avoid fighting while Volibear builds stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm with basic attacks. Once the stacks fall off, slow his movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither, then hit him with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. In small skirmishes, you can also activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Volibear goes in.
Volibear.laning: Near your turret, don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave; save mana for fights and gank follow-ups. If Volibear’s pressure makes even Q last-hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Volibear.phase: Nasus is weak early, so focus on building Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks instead of fighting Volibear. From the mid to late game, once your stacks are built and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is available, the matchup favors Nasus; look to fight or pressure turrets then.
Volibear.teamfight: Don’t go in alone; wait until your team starts the fight, then engage. If Volibear goes for your backline, catch him with Nasus W Wither, then use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Activating Nasus R Fury of the Sands at the start of a teamfight lets you deal damage over time around you and use Q more often.
Volibear.watch: If Volibear approaches with Volibear Q Thundering Smash active, watch out for the stun on his empowered basic attack and let its duration run out beyond his attack range. When you see the mark from Volibear E Sky Splitter, move to the side to avoid its damage and slow. If Volibear R Stormbringer is available, watch for a dive even under your turret.

Yasuo.build: Build armor first to prepare for Yasuo Q Steel Tempest and Yasuo R Last Breath, his main sources of damage. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade deals magic damage, so armor won’t block it, but include at least one defensive item such as Dead Man’s Plate even if you focus on damage.
Yasuo.combo: Use W to keep him on the E area, then hit Q after E’s armor reduction applies.
Yasuo.escape: The moment after Yasuo sends out his tornado is your chance to engage. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t go deep just because he used it once; look for an opportunity with crowd control before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back.
Yasuo.fight: Keep your distance and avoid fighting early; start trading after Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield disappears. When Yasuo has briefly lost his way to knock you up after sending out a tornado, slow his movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither and fight.
Yasuo.laning: Keeping a thin wave on your side of the lane reduces the number of minions Yasuo can use as stepping stones to approach with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. Near your turret, don’t use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave; build stacks by last-hitting with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If his pressure makes even Q last-hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Yasuo.phase: Nasus gets strong from the mid to late game, once he has built stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so survive the early game and then choose to fight or apply split-push pressure.
Yasuo.teamfight: Don’t lead the fight alone; engage after your team starts it. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry to pin them down, then hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while the target is on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Activating Nasus R Fury of the Sands lets you deal damage over time around you and use Q more often.
Yasuo.watch: After Yasuo lands Yasuo Q Steel Tempest twice, his next tornado will knock you up, so watch for the sound and visual effect and dodge to the side. Yasuo can use minions to approach with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, and once he catches you, Nasus has no escape skill and can easily be hit repeatedly.

Yone.build: Even if you build damage, get at least one defensive item such as Dead Man’s Plate first. Yone deals a mix of physical and magic damage, so consider both armor and magic resistance instead of focusing on one type of resistance. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone.
Yone.combo: After Yone goes in, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Slow Yone with Nasus W Wither to keep him on Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike after his armor is reduced.
Yone.escape: Look for an opening after the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel disappears. Don’t go in as soon as Yone E Soul Unbound is down; check his other mobility tools too. In particular, the window before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back is your chance to engage.
Yone.fight: Keep your distance while the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel is ready. After Yone engages, slow his movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither. In small skirmishes, activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands after Yone goes in, then hit him with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while he’s on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Yone.laning: Don’t push the lane too hard early; let the wave come to you and last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Near your turret, use Nasus E Spirit Fire to push the wave so you don’t miss last-hits, while saving mana for fights and jungle intervention. If Yone’s pressure makes even Nasus Q Siphoning Strike last-hits difficult, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Yone.phase: Nasus gets strong from the mid to late game, once he has built stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Later on, you can choose to pressure turrets with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike in addition to joining teamfights.
Yone.teamfight: Don’t lead the fight alone; go in after your team engages, and slow Yone with Nasus W Wither if he goes for your backline. Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield doesn’t grow, and make sure you aren’t standing alone at the very back of your formation before Yone R Fate Sealed. Activate Nasus R Fury of the Sands, then keep hitting with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while the target is on Nasus E Spirit Fire.
Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions, his tornado is ready, so keep your distance until the stacks disappear. Nasus has no skill to escape on his own, so it’s dangerous to get caught by an engage chained from Yone E Soul Unbound into Yone R Fate Sealed. Also account for the extra damage when Yone returns after using Yone E Soul Unbound to deal damage.

Yorick.build: Build armor first to withstand the physical damage from Yorick Q Last Rites and his Mist Walkers. Yorick E Mourning Mist and Yorick R Eulogy of the Isles deal magic damage and damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone. If the healing from Yorick Q Last Rites is a problem, fit in Executioner’s Calling and apply Grievous Wounds with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Yorick.combo: When you get a chance to close in on Yorick, use Nasus W Wither → Nasus E Spirit Fire → Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Use Nasus W Wither to keep Yorick in the area, lower his armor with Nasus E Spirit Fire, then land Nasus Q Siphoning Strike.
Yorick.escape: Dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist, then engage while that ability is down. If Yorick W Dark Procession is down too, you have a chance to close in without worrying about being trapped by the wall, and Yorick has no skill to create distance on his own.
Yorick.fight: Avoid direct fights early and build last-hit stacks with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist and clear the Mist Walkers; while Yorick E Mourning Mist is down, move forward to farm or engage. When you’re close, slow Yorick’s movement and attack speed with Nasus W Wither.
Yorick.laning: If Yorick pushes the lane, don’t force a push back; last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike near your turret. Using Nasus E Spirit Fire here can push the wave and make you miss last-hits, so save mana for fights and gank follow-ups. If Yorick’s pressure makes last-hitting impossible, ask for a jungle gank or a lane swap.
Yorick.phase: From the mid game onward, you gain strength once you’ve built stacks and can use Nasus R Fury of the Sands. Later on, Nasus has the advantage after surviving the early game and building stacks, so fight with your accumulated stacks or pressure turrets.
Yorick.teamfight: Don’t lead the fight alone; engage after your team starts it. Use Nasus W Wither on the enemy carry, then hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike while the target is on Nasus E Spirit Fire. Activating Nasus R Fury of the Sands lets you deal damage over time around you and use Nasus Q Siphoning Strike more often.
Yorick.watch: Yorick E Mourning Mist slows, marks, and deals damage based on your maximum health, so dodge when the orb comes your way. If you get trapped in Yorick W Dark Procession, you can attack the wall to break it. If the Maiden of the Mist is marked, move away from Yorick himself.
